brief: BTIG's technical strategy note argues breadth and credit divergences since August are unsustainable. The S&P 500 sits within 2% of a 52-week high while under 50% of its members trade above their 200-day average, and 52-week lows have outnumbered highs for nine straight days. Since 1990 that combination has occurred only in Dec 1999-Jan 2000, and now Sep 2026. In the 1999-2000 analog, equal-weight fell 16% while the S&P 500 rose 8%, then the two reversed roles: the S&P 500 fell 17% while equal-weight rallied 20%. Separately, it has been 213 trading days since the last 80%-or-greater NYSE downside-volume day (average 21 a year, never fewer than 5), so BTIG expects a high-correlation selloff soon. Credit corroborates this: CCC spreads have widened 11 of the last 14 days toward 2022 levels, high-yield spreads are widening against investment-grade, and both high-yield and investment-grade tech CDS are diverging from equities, with Meta bonds falling as its stock rises. Short-term direction hinges on Iran de-escalation: a deal would lift the hardest-hit sectors (discretionary, financials, REITs, utilities) most while tech/AI lags, without reversing the primary uptrend in Treasury yields, decoupled from sideways crude. Bounce candidates: BURL, EAT, YETI, GOLF.

cards.claim: Mega-cap tech ETFs outperformed broad and equal-weight benchmarks last week, with SMH +5.9%, QQQ +3.2%, and SPY +1.3% versus RSP -0.6% and IWM -0.8%.
Fewer than 50% of S&P 500 names trade above their 200-day moving average, a breadth reading not triggered since 2000.
cards.anchor: Two breadth metrics triggered unseen since 2000: <50% of SPX names above their 200 DMA

cards.claim: The S&P 500 has posted more 52-week lows than 52-week highs for nine straight days even as the index trades near its highs.
cards.anchor: more 52wk lows than highs for nine straight days—both with the index near highs.

cards.claim: Since 1990 there have been only 25 other trading days with less than 50% of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day moving average while the index was closer to a 52-week high than it was as of the note.
cards.anchor: Since 1990 there have only been 25 other days that had less than 50% of S&P 500 stocks above their 200 DMA

cards.claim: All 25 of those prior low-breadth-near-highs occurrences took place between 1998 and 2000.
cards.anchor: All of those occurred between 1998 and 2000.

cards.claim: Since 1990, the only periods with nine straight days of more 52-week lows than highs while the S&P 500 was within 2% of a 52-week high were December 1999, January 2000, and now September 2026.
cards.anchor: within 2% of a 52wk high: Dec. ’99, Jan. ’00, Sep. ’26.

cards.claim: From July 1999 through February 2000, the equal-weight S&P 500 fell 16% while the cap-weighted S&P 500 rose about 8%.
cards.anchor: the equal-weight S&P 500 fell 16% while the SPX went up ~8%.

cards.claim: After that divergence, the two reversed roles, with the S&P 500 falling 17% into late December while the equal-weight S&P 500 rallied 20% over the same span.
cards.anchor: they reversed roles with the SPX falling -17% into late December while the SPW rallied 20% over the same span.

cards.claim: It has been 213 trading days since the last 80%-or-greater NYSE downside volume day.
cards.anchor: It’s now been 213 trading days since the last 80%+ NYSE downside volume day.

cards.claim: The average calendar year sees 21 days of 80%-or-greater NYSE downside volume, and no year on record has had fewer than five.
cards.anchor: The average calendar year sees 21 such days, and we have never seen a year with fewer than five.

cards.claim: BTIG expects a correlation-one, high-correlation market selloff to occur soon.
cards.anchor: we continue to think the clock is ticking and we see one sooner than later.

cards.claim: WTI crude has traded sideways since mid-March even as the 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.50%.
cards.anchor: crude has essentially been moving sideways since mid-March, while 30yr yields have continued to march higher from ~5% to 5.50%.

cards.claim: BTIG says the primary uptrend in Treasury yields remains firmly intact regardless of a near-term pullback from Middle East de-escalation.
cards.anchor: the primary upward trend in rates remains firmly intact.

cards.claim: BTIG says short-term equity market direction hinges on whether a real de-escalation with Iran is reached.
cards.anchor: Short-term direction hinges on Iran de-escalation.

cards.claim: If a Middle East deal is reached, the hardest-hit sectors, discretionary, financials, REITs and utilities, will likely rebound the most while tech and AI stocks lag.
cards.anchor: hardest-hit sectors (discretionary, financials, REITs, Utilities) will likely rebound most while tech/AI lags.

cards.claim: If there is any resolution in the Middle East, the consumer discretionary sector is the group BTIG expects to rebound the hardest.
cards.anchor: if there is any sort of resolution in the Middle East, this is also the group that likely rebounds the hardest.

cards.claim: BTIG names Burlington Stores, Brinker, Yeti Holdings and Acushnet Holdings as bounce candidates that have been hit hard but are coming into strong support levels.
cards.anchor: These names have all been hit hard but coming into strong support levels

cards.claim: CCC-rated high-yield spreads have widened in 11 of the last 14 trading days, approaching 2022 levels.

cards.claim: CCC-rated high-yield spreads have surged nearly 300 basis points from their May level.
cards.anchor: CCC spreads have surged nearly 300bps from May.
